free_tier.stated: The free tier is static sites only: 'Static Sites | Free | CDN: Global, Bandwidth: 100 GB, Builds: ~20s, Sites: Unlimited | 0 EUR/mo', plus object storage '5 GB free'. Web services start at 'Nano | vCPU: 0.1, RAM: 256 MB, Disk: 1 GB, Bandwidth: 100 GB | 3 EUR/mo | 0.0041 EUR/hr' and 'Starter | vCPU: 0.5, RAM: 512 MB, Disk: 5 GB, Bandwidth: 1 TB | 5 EUR/mo | 0.0068 EUR/hr'.

egress.terms: 'Static Sites | Free | CDN: Global, Bandwidth: 100 GB, Builds: ~20s, Sites: Unlimited | 0 EUR/mo | 0.0000 EUR/hr', quoted from the monthly and hourly table

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: hourly billing at EUR 0.0041 for a 0.1 vCPU service means a six-hour job costs about EUR 0.03, so this is a cheap place to park a short-lived web endpoint beside the free static site.
limits_note: the free tier carries static hosting only, so the first wall is EUR 3 for a 0.1 vCPU web service.

notes: Aggregator claim checked: free-for.dev says 'European PaaS with automated deployments from GitHub for web services or static sites (1 web 0.1 vCPU/256 MB free), managed PostgreSQL and Valkey (30 days for free), Transactional Email (3,000 emails/month free), S3 compatible storage (5 GB/free)'. The free web service is wrong: the vendor table marks Static Sites as the 0 EUR row and prices the 0.1 vCPU web service at EUR 3 a month, so a reader would build against a free tier that does not exist. The 5 GB of object storage is real. The 30-day free database was not confirmed: the managed PostgreSQL rows on the same table start at EUR 3.
